item.title: Governing Artificial Intelligence Use in Business Education: Risk and Prevention
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the governance and management of artificial intelligence applications within business education settings. The call addresses concerns related to risks associated with AI use and explores preventive measures and strategies for responsible AI governance in educational contexts.

item.title: The Hidden Costs of Technological Progress: Risks, Governance, and Sustainability in the Transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the often-overlooked negative externalities and challenges accompanying technological progress, particularly in the shift toward Industry 5.0. Rather than celebrating innovation uncritically, the call invites research that interrogates the hidden risks, governance gaps, and sustainability concerns that emerge during major industrial transitions.

The special issue seeks contributions that address how societies can navigate technological change while minimizing harm, establishing effective governance mechanisms, and ensuring sustainable outcomes. It welcomes interdisciplinary perspectives on the complex relationship between technological advancement, environmental protection, social welfare, and economic viability.

Appel publié par Technology in Society. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Risks associated with technological advancement and digital transformation
  • Governance frameworks for emerging technologies
  • Sustainability implications of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0
  • Environmental and social costs of technological progress
  • Policy and regulatory approaches to managing technological transitions
  • Ethical considerations in technology deployment
  • Human and organizational impacts of industrial transformation

Timeline

  • January 18, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Financial inclusion strategies, technology, and risk management: emerging trends and global perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Juan Piñeiro Chousa, Santiago de Compostela University

Financial systems face evolving risks from climate change, digitalisation, and new financial ecosystems that challenge existing supervision and policy frameworks. Advanced technologies like artificial intelligence, big data analytics, and satellite systems enhance risk identification and monitoring, yet introduce new technological and cybersecurity threats. Sustainable finance and financial inclusion have emerged as instruments for managing long-term risks and strengthening financial system resilience, though questions persist regarding data quality and greenwashing.

This special issue seeks theoretical and empirical research examining the challenges and opportunities arising from the convergence of technology, sustainability, and financial inclusion. Contributions should adopt financial and risk management perspectives, with particular interest in studies addressing implications for financial stability, prudential supervision, and public policy design.

Appel publié par The Journal of Risk Finance. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The use of satellite and alternative data in financial risk assessment
  • Financial technologies, artificial intelligence, and emerging risks
  • Technological, modelling, and cybersecurity risks in the financial system
  • Sustainable finance, capital allocation, and systemic risk
  • Financial inclusion, digitalisation, and resilience to economic shocks
  • Decentralised finance (DeFi) and risks to financial stability
  • Regenerative finance (ReFi) and long-term risk management
  • Blockchain, tokenisation, and traceability in sustainability and green finance projects
  • Regulatory and supervisory frameworks for sustainable finance, fintech, decentralised finance (DeFi), and regenerative finance (ReFi)
  • Applications of big data, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in sustainable finance
  • Supervision, regulation, and macroprudential policies in response to emerging risks

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • December 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Leadership and Governance in Complex Learning Systems: Risk, Knowledge and Entrepreneurship
item.content:encoded:
Enis Elezi, University of Westminster

Knowledge-intensive organisations face mounting complexity from resource constraints, digitalisation, accountability demands, and geopolitical pressures. Existing research on these challenges remains fragmented across disciplinary silos and often lacks systemic understanding of how these institutions observe, interpret and respond to complexity.

This special issue integrates typically isolated scholarly conversations about leadership, governance, risk, knowledge and entrepreneurship within a cybernetic framework. It explores the interconnected processes of observation, communication, decision and learning that enable organisations to adapt and remain viable across sectors including universities, health systems, research institutes and public agencies.

Appel publié par Kybernetes. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Leadership and governance as systemic architectures of observation, decision and learning
  • Enterprise-wide risk management, knowledge management and entrepreneurship as interconnected cybernetic processes
  • Cross-sector analyses of universities, health systems, research institutes, public agencies and professional service firms as complex learning systems
  • Reflexive and second-order perspectives on how organisations construct and revise their own governance arrangements
  • Theory-as-method applications using cybernetics, systems thinking or complexity frameworks

Timeline

  • January 26, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • December 26, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Digital and AI Transformation in Insurance
item.content:encoded:
Anja Grujovic-Vischer, The Geneva Association

Ruo Jia, Peking University

Zhiyu Quan, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

Digital technologies, artificial intelligence, data science, InsurTechs, and automation are reshaping how risks are identified, priced, mitigated, transferred, managed, and regulated. These developments raise important questions not only for re/insurers and regulators, but also for the wider research community.

This special issue welcomes high-quality empirical, experimental, policy-oriented, and practice-based contributions that deepen our understanding of digital and AI transformation in insurance and related risk-transfer markets. We particularly encourage submissions that speak to broad academic debates while offering clear implications for insurance markets, insurers, consumers, regulators, and society.

Appel publié par The Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance Issues and Practice. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital technologies and their impact on insurance
  • Artificial intelligence applications in insurance
  • Data science in risk identification and pricing
  • InsurTechs and automation in insurance
  • Risk mitigation and transfer in digital contexts
  • Insurance regulation in the digital age
  • Consumer implications of digital transformation
  • Societal impacts of AI in insurance

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline
